concepts.statement_en: Plan a response around permission, the visit purpose and the person’s concern.
Explore reasons for the response without assuming an uncooperative motive.
Identify when to seek supervisor or emergency support; do not force entry.
Respond with patience and a calm voice rather than blame or interruption.
Offer an appropriate private and safe setting with the resident’s agreement.
Ask about the concern, listen, summarize and invite correction.
Explore the resident’s desired outcome and realistic alternatives.
Agree a solution without forced consent or unsupported promises.
Confirm the action, responsible person and follow-up time.
Share necessary factual information with the appropriate colleague without humiliation.
Review one’s response and identify a specific improvement.
Apply the communication and review process in household work with supervision.
